description: Image box, app bar, modal layer and status bar: cases shared by every reader of the contract (schema 9.9.0). Written by hand; numbers are logical pixels. `tokens` are the values of the built-in theme the rows use (spacing steps, the `pill` radius) — a reader takes them from the theme, the rows only say which numbers the expectations were computed with. `ratioCases`: the field `Image.aspectRatio` as it stands in a document (the key is absent in the row «no field») → the ratio width / height the reader uses, given as a pair (compare the quotient). `ratioDocumentCases`: is the value accepted by the JSON Schema (`schema`) and, when it is, which validator code refuses to publish it (`code`, null: none). `imageBoxCases`: `width` is the width of the node box — named by `style.width` or given by the parent; `style` holds the named `height` / `minHeight` / `maxHeight` (absent: not named); the box of the image is `expect`, and `byRatio` says whether the proportion was used at all. `paintCases`: where the picture with the natural ratio `natural` (width / height of the file) lies in the box for `fit` — a rectangle in box coordinates, centred; with `cover` it sticks out of the box and is clipped. `radiusCases`: the effective corner radius of a box (named radius clamped to half of the smaller side) and whether the box is a circle. `circleCases`: which style fields the «Circle» shortcut of the builder writes for a side (`pill`: the value of the token, `maxRadius`: the limit of an own radius). `appBarCases`: `width` is the content width of the bar, `actionSides` — sides of the VISIBLE actions in document order, `titleNatural` — the natural width of the title block (the longer of title and subtitle on one line); `expect` is in READING order from the start edge: `leading` / `trailing` — widths of the side zones with their gap, `titleStart` and `actionStarts` — offsets from the start edge. `rtlLeft` (where present) is the same layout as offsets from the LEFT edge in a right-to-left script: left = width − start − size. `modalCases`: `viewport` is the area the host gave the screen, `contentHeight` — the height of the layer content measured at the layer width, `margin` — the window margin (`center.margin`); `expect` is the rectangle of the layer and whether its content scrolls inside it. `placementCases` / `statusBarCases`: how a reader reads the two screen fields (`null`: no request). `documentCases`: a tiny document described by `screens` (first is the initial one unless `initial` names another; `appBarChildren` puts an app bar with these child types on the first screen) → accepted by the JSON Schema or not, and the validator codes it must report (empty: publishable). `shownCases`: the stack AFTER the change (last frame is the top), what happened to it, and the «screen shown» event the host must get — exactly these keys: `modalPlacement` and `statusBarIcons` appear only when the screen names them. `screenAppBarCases` (clarification before release, the screen anatomy): the types of the children of a screen root in document order → the index of the child that is the APP BAR ZONE, or null; `hidden` says which children a condition hides now — it never moves the zone to another node (`zoneNow` false: the zone is empty). `zoneCases`: the zones of a screen in its own coordinates (from its top edge). Input: `height` — the height the host gave (for a modal layer, `shrink` true — the AVAILABLE height), `appBarHeight` — the box of the bar with its own padding (the key is absent when there is no zone), `padding` — top and bottom padding of the screen root, `gap` — the gap of the screen, `bodyContentHeight` — the flow of the visible body children with the pull of the FIRST one not applied (absent — no visible children), `firstPull`, `scrollTop`. Expectation: `appBar` — its box, the same at any scroll; `body` — the area everything scrolled is clipped by; `contentTop` — the top of the first body child at this scroll; `contentHeight` — the length of what scrolls, measured from the top of the body area. `screenRuleCases`: a dotted path in `x-style.layout.screen` → its value; rows no geometry can say (background, clipping, the web block without its own height). `modalAreaCases`: the area of a modal layer is the area the host gave the screen — `frame` and `insets` describe a HOST, `area` is what it gave, `expect` is the window in FRAME coordinates.

description916: Groups added by schema 9.16.0 (the rows above are untouched, except ONE document row: «three actions do not fit beside a title» is now accepted by the structure — an app bar holds up to three children, the leading node and two actions — and refused by the validator). Written out as plain numbers; logical pixels. `appBarLeadingCases`: the zones of an app bar with a node in the LEADING zone — the input of `appBarCases` plus `leadingNatural` (the natural outer width of the VISIBLE leading node, or its named `style.width`; absent — no visible leading node, `showBack` applies) and `titleAlign` as it stands in the document (absent — no field). `expect.leadingWidth` is what stands in the leading zone WITHOUT the gap (the node clamped to half of the bar, the back square, or zero), `expect.leading` — with the gap. `rtlLeft` — the same layout measured from the LEFT edge in a right-to-left script: `leading` is the left edge of what stands in the leading zone (null — nothing). `appBarLeadingShownCases`: what is drawn in the leading zone — `nodeVisible` null: the bar has no leading node; true / false: its condition. `appBarChildrenCases`: which child of the bar is the leading node and which are actions, by index in document order (visibility is not counted here). `appBarPlaceCases`: where a child put into the bar goes — the answer shared by the validator and the builder. `appBar916DocumentCases`: is the document accepted by the JSON Schema (`schema`) and, when it is, which validator codes refuse to publish it. `appBarChildren` — children of the bar, `bodyChildren` — children of the screen root next to a bar, `appBarProps` — extra props of the bar. `glyphCases`: the own size of a drawing (`glyphSize`) on an «Icon» and an «IconButton». `typography` is the measured font token of the size word (font size, line-height multiplier) in the built-in theme, `padding` — the padding on ONE side (the block padding of the button of that size, or the named one), `border` — the border width on one side, `style` — the NAMED `width` / `height` of the node. `expect`: `glyph` — the side of the drawing, `content` — the content box, `box` — the node box, `own` — whether the number was read. Compare to two decimals: the line of `bodyM` is 14 × 1.4286. `appBar916RuleCases`: a dotted path in `x-style.layout` → its value.

screenTopNote: Groups added by schema 9.19.0, theme 3 — the body under the app bar (`Screen.props.bodyTop`) and the top safe inset the reader adds (the rows above are untouched). Written out by hand as plain numbers; logical pixels. `bodyTopCases`: the field as it stands in a document (`value` absent in the row «no field») → the word the reader uses. `topZoneCases`: the types of the children of a screen root in document order, the width class of the screen box, the field `widePlacement` of the navigation bar where it is named and the children a condition hides now → who owns the app bar zone (`owner`) and whether the body of a screen with `bodyTop: 'screenTop'` starts at the top edge of the screen (`atScreenTop`): never under an own navigation strip. `screenTopZoneCases`: the input of `zoneCases` plus `bodyTop` (absent — no field) and `safeTop` (the top inset of the platform; absent — zero) → the zones in screen coordinates from the PHYSICAL top: `appBar` is the box of the bar WITH the inset inside it and `contentTop` is where its content starts; `body` is the area the scrolled content is clipped by; `bottom` — as in the bottom-zone table. `screenTopPressCases`: `screen` is such an input with the width of the screen, the direction of the script and the side paddings of the root (the box of the app bar stands inside them: left = start padding in LTR, end padding in RTL); `point` is in screen coordinates from the top-LEFT corner → the ZONE that takes the press. `screenTopRuleCases`: a dotted path in `x-style.layout` → its value; rows no geometry can say. `screenTopDocumentCases`: the props of a screen root (and `propsOn` where named) → accepted by the JSON Schema or not, and the validator codes (empty: publishable).

safeTopModalNote: The top safe inset the reader adds (`safeTopValueCases`) and a modal layer (`x-style.layout.safeTop.modal`). The host gave the reader the WHOLE `frame` and the inset `safeTop`; the layer area is the frame below the inset: the scrim covers the inset, a sheet is no taller than the area below it, a window is centred in it. The bottom inset is not taken from the area (a sheet carries it inside its content, a window has none), so the rows have none. `margin` is the window margin (`center.margin`); `expect` is the rectangle of the layer in FRAME coordinates, from the physical top, and its vertical centre.
